note: People born in Puerto Rico are United States citizens; the United States issues no national identity card (6 U.S.C. § 554), so they hold none. Cards issued locally are left to the United States package, with the driver's license.

sources.title: United States Code, 2023 edition (govinfo.gov), 8 U.S.C. § 1402, Persons born in Puerto Rico on or after April 11, 1899
sources.said: All persons born in Puerto Rico on or after January 13, 1941, and subject to the jurisdiction of the United States, are citizens of the United States at birth.

sources.title: LII, 6 U.S. Code § 554, National identification system not authorized (Pub. L. 107-296, title XV, § 1514)
sources.said: 6 U.S. Code § 554 - National identification system not authorized ... Nothing in this chapter shall be construed to authorize the development of a national identification system or card.
